steps.message:
Our CEI billing is going into the council package and DeLuca wants our fee position on the assignment as a whole before it goes over, with the contract time now running to November. Tell me where we stand against the ceiling and what that means for what we can properly put to the City before the package goes. Our invoices to the City and the fee proposal are on the share with the rest of the project record.

One memo to DeLuca over my signature as Project Manager, dated May 15, 2026. Save it as /filesystem/CEI_Fee_Ceiling_Position.docx

(Normal) Dear Mr. DeLuca:
(Normal) Larkspur Civil Group, Inc. is pleased to submit this proposal for Construction Engineering and Inspection (CEI) services for the Wren Parkway Widening & Pecan Creek Bridge Replacement, City Project No. WP-2401. As the designer of record, our firm has developed a detailed understanding of the design intent, the contract documents, the geotechnical record, and the environmental and permitting framework governing the work. That continuity provides a direct, low-risk transition into the construction-phase administration of the Contract and positions the City for a defensible, well-documented project record from Notice to Proceed through Substantial Completion.
(Normal) Our lump-sum fee for the CEI scope described in the sections that follow is $761,800, inclusive of an itemized reimbursable expense allowance and priced against the original contract time of 607 calendar days ending at Substantial Completion on September 4, 2026. This CEI fee is separate from and additional to the previously executed design-phase professional services fee of $1,384,500.
(Normal) The scope, staffing, schedule assumptions, and fee build-up are presented in Sections 1 through 7 below. Exhibit A sets out the hourly rate schedule by classification for the CEI project team, and Exhibit B sets out the reimbursable expense rate schedule.
(Normal) The proposal is priced against the original Contract time. Any executed time extensions, changes in the character of the work, or material expansions of scope (including, but not limited to, added phases, added intersections, or extended field-office operations beyond Substantial Completion) will be handled by written fee amendment prior to performance of the added effort.
(Normal) We appreciate the City's continued confidence in Larkspur Civil Group, and we are prepared to mobilize the CEI team immediately upon Notice to Proceed to the construction contractor.
(Normal) Respectfully submitted,
(Normal) LARKSPUR CIVIL GROUP, INC.

(Normal) 1.  Firm Profile
(Normal) 1.1  Overview
(Normal) Larkspur Civil Group, Inc. is a Texas-registered civil engineering consulting firm (Texas Board of Professional Engineers and Land Surveyors Firm Registration No. F-9421), incorporated in Delaware in 2003 and licensed to practice engineering in Texas since inception. The firm provides planning, design, and construction engineering and inspection services to municipal, county, and state clients across Central and South Texas, with core practice areas in roadway widening and reconstruction, minor and major bridge replacement, drainage and detention design, and construction phase administration for owner clients.
(Normal) Larkspur maintains a two-office footprint:
[TABLE]
Office | Address | Phone | Staff
Austin (Headquarters) | 4225 Windsor Bluff Drive, Suite 800, Austin, TX 78745 | (512) 555-0180 | 41
San Antonio (Branch) | 220 W. Fannin Street, Suite 400, San Antonio, TX 78205 | (210) 555-0122 | 21
Total |  |  | 62
[/TABLE]
(Normal) Roughly two-thirds of Larkspur's staff of 62 are technical (registered engineers, engineers-in-training, designers, and field inspection personnel), with the balance in project controls, contracts administration, survey, and administrative support. FY 2025 gross revenue was $14.8 million, with recurring municipal transportation and CEI clients representing the majority of the firm's book of work.
(Normal) 1.2  Relevant Experience
(Normal) The proposed principal-in-charge, project manager, and resident engineer for WP-2401 have collectively delivered CEI services on more than fifteen Central Texas roadway and bridge projects of comparable scale over the past decade, including three prestressed girder bridge replacements on drilled shaft foundations over similar karstic limestone stratigraphy. The structural lead is the designer of record for the WP-2401 bridge and will remain assigned through construction, providing an unbroken chain of engineering judgment from design through in-place acceptance.
(Normal) 1.3  Continuity from Design
(Normal) Because Larkspur prepared the Issued-for-Construction documents, the CEI team begins the assignment with:
(List Bullet) Full working familiarity with the sealed 90% and 100% plans, specifications, and calculations of record;
(List Bullet) Direct access to the sealed geotechnical report prepared by Redoak Geoscience LLC, including boring log B-7 at Bent 2 and the pinnacled-rock variability note in Section 5.2 of that report;
(List Bullet) The floodplain, USACE, and environmental permit conditions previously secured for the crossing at Pecan Creek;
(List Bullet) Established working relationships with the City Engineer's office, with utility owners along the corridor, and with the independent materials testing laboratory to be retained by the City.
(Normal) This continuity is expected to reduce mobilization risk, shorten review turnaround times for submittals and RFIs, and enable prompt engineering judgments on differing site conditions, means-and-methods proposals, and constructability questions as they arise.
(Normal) 2.  Understanding of the Project
(Normal) The Wren Parkway Widening & Pecan Creek Bridge Replacement project is a 2.4-mile municipal transportation improvement extending from the intersection of Old Millican Road (Sta. 100+00) to the intersection of McKinney Boulevard (Sta. 226+00). The work consists of two integrated packages:
(Normal) Roadway Widening (Sta. 100+00 to Sta. 226+00).  Reconstruction and widening of the existing 2-lane rural section to a 4-lane divided urban section with 8-foot outside shoulders and 6-foot sidewalks. The work includes full-depth pavement, curb and gutter, storm drainage (twelve trunk runs designed to the 25-year rational-method basis), traffic signals at Old Millican Road and McKinney Boulevard, streetlighting, and roadside safety hardware. Retaining wall Reach R-2 (Sta. 151+50 to Sta. 154+00) provides fill support at the sanitary sewer conflict area.
(Normal) Bridge Replacement (Sta. 167+00 to Sta. 169+85).  Complete replacement of the 1962 two-span steel girder bridge over Pecan Creek with a new 3-span, 285-foot prestressed concrete girder bridge continuous for live load, founded on twelve 48-inch drilled shafts socketed a minimum of 8 feet into sound limestone at 40 ksf allowable end bearing. The scour countermeasure at the abutments is sized per FHWA HEC-23 Design Guideline 11.
(Normal) The construction is scheduled for competitive-bid award to a general contractor selected from the November 12, 2024 bid opening, with Notice to Proceed anticipated in early January 2025 and Substantial Completion set at September 4, 2026 — a Contract time of 607 calendar days.
(Normal) The federal-aid participation (STP 2024(041) MK) requires that construction records, prevailing-wage compliance, and DBE participation be documented in accordance with federal-aid procedures throughout the life of the Contract.
(Normal) 3.  Project Team and Organization
(Normal) Larkspur will assign the following professionals to the WP-2401 CEI assignment. Each named individual is committed to the project for the duration of the original Contract time; substitutions of key personnel will be made only with the prior written concurrence of the City Engineer.

(Normal) 3.2  Key Personnel
(Normal) Elena Vasquez, PE — Principal-in-Charge (Texas P.E. License No. TX PE #92451). Ms. Vasquez holds ultimate professional and contractual responsibility for the CEI assignment. She signs all Larkspur deliverables to the City requiring an engineering seal, provides internal quality-assurance review of claim recommendations and change-order dispositions, and is the final internal authority on Contract interpretation questions elevated by the Project Manager. Anticipated involvement: level effort throughout the project with peaks at NTP, major milestones, and Substantial Completion.
(Normal) Marcus Okafor, PE — Project Manager (Texas P.E. License No. TX PE #108772). Mr. Okafor is the day-to-day Larkspur point of contact for the City Engineer. He is responsible for the CEI budget and schedule, monthly progress reporting to the City, coordination of the technical team, and authorship of the City-facing memoranda that carry the Engineer's determinations on claims, change orders, and pay applications. Anticipated involvement: level effort throughout, approximately 40% of Mr. Okafor's chargeable time on WP-2401.
(Normal) Dana Whitfield, PE — Resident Engineer (Texas P.E. License No. TX PE #115993). Ms. Whitfield leads the field office and holds the Resident Engineer role for the duration of construction. She is responsible for the RFI and submittal logs, the daily-report record, meeting minutes for the weekly progress meetings, pay-application review and certification, and the interface with the independent materials testing laboratory. Anticipated involvement: full-time equivalent, on-site presence at the field office throughout the earthwork, drilled-shaft, and bridge substructure phases; balance of time between field and Austin office during pavement and closeout phases.
(Normal) Priya Raman, PE — Structural Lead (Texas P.E. License No. TX PE #121408). Ms. Raman was the engineer of record for the design of the new 3-span bridge and remains the structural lead for construction. She reviews all structural submittals (prestressed girders, drilled shaft installation, deck reinforcement, expansion joints, bearings), authors the sealed responses to RFIs raising structural-design questions, and provides load-rating and constructability review for the existing 1962 bridge deconstruction and any temporary works interfacing with the new structure. Anticipated involvement: approximately 25–30% of Ms. Raman's chargeable time during substructure and superstructure phases, tapering thereafter.
(Normal) Tom Herrera, EIT — Field Inspector (Texas E.I.T. Certificate No. TX EIT #43127). Mr. Herrera is the lead field inspector for the assignment. He authors the daily inspection reports, monitors compliance with the traffic control plan, witnesses concrete placements and material sampling, and records quantities for pay-application backup. Two additional Field Inspector II personnel from Larkspur's field staff will be assigned as workload requires. Anticipated involvement: full-time equivalent while active construction is underway.
(Normal) Janet Kolb — Contracts Administrator (Larkspur — Austin office). Ms. Kolb maintains the change-order log, the executed-contract file, the bond and insurance certificates, the DBE participation ledger, and the monthly invoicing to the City. She provides support to the Project Manager and Principal-in-Charge on federal-aid compliance recordkeeping and prevailing-wage documentation. Anticipated involvement: approximately 15–20% of Ms. Kolb's chargeable time throughout the project.
(Normal) 3.3  Reporting Relationships
(Normal) Ms. Vasquez reports to the City Engineer on matters of professional judgment and final Larkspur position. Mr. Okafor conducts the day-to-day business of the assignment with the City Engineer and communicates in writing on all matters affecting Contract price, time, or quality. Ms. Whitfield reports internally to Mr. Okafor and, in the field, works directly with the Contractor's project manager and superintendent on the routine business of construction administration. Ms. Raman reports to Ms. Vasquez on matters of structural professional judgment and to Mr. Okafor on schedule and budget for the CEI assignment. Ms. Kolb reports to Ms. Vasquez.
(Normal) 4.  Scope of Services
(Normal) The CEI scope of services set out in this section is organized as it will appear in the labor-hour build-up of Section 5. All services are provided to the standard of care applicable to CEI consultants in the State of Texas.
(Normal) 4.1  Task 1 — Project Management & Contract Administration
(Normal) Larkspur will provide overall management of the CEI assignment, including internal team coordination, monthly invoicing to the City, maintenance of the executed-contract file and change-order log, coordination with the City Engineer's office on Contract interpretation questions, and quality-assurance review of all deliverables that leave the office over Larkspur's letterhead. Federal-aid recordkeeping is performed at this task level, including the DBE participation ledger and the file of certified payrolls received from the Contractor. Monthly Larkspur invoices to the City are supported by classification-level hour detail and reimbursable receipts.
(Normal) 4.2  Task 2 — Preconstruction, Mobilization & Baseline Review
(Normal) Immediately following award of the construction Contract and prior to Notice to Proceed, Larkspur will (a) prepare the CEI mobilization plan and field-office set-up; (b) attend the preconstruction conference with the Contractor and City; (c) review the Contractor's baseline schedule for compliance with the specification requirements and reasonableness of logic, durations, and calendar assumptions; (d) review the Contractor's schedule of values against the bid tabulation and confirm balance across the 118 bid items; (e) issue the initial submittal register with target dates aligned to procurement lead times; and (f) confirm receipt of executed bonds, insurance certificates, and traffic-control coordination with local emergency services.
(Normal) 4.3  Task 3 — On-Site Inspection & Daily Reporting
(Normal) Larkspur will provide field inspection during all active hours of construction. Daily inspection reports (Larkspur form DR-####) will be prepared each work day and issued to the Contractor and City by close of business the following business day. Reports document weather, crew and equipment counts by trade, work performed by station and item, materials received, tests witnessed, safety observations, and any events materially affecting Contract time or quality. Field inspectors witness all concrete placements, structural steel and prestressed girder handling operations, drilled shaft installations, subgrade proof-rolls, and utility ties, and record quantities for pay-application backup as work is put in place.
(Normal) 4.4  Task 4 — Submittal & Shop Drawing Review
(Normal) Larkspur will maintain the submittal register (Larkspur form SUB-###) and route each submittal for review by the appropriate technical discipline. Review disciplines include structural (girders, drilled shafts, bearings, joints, deck reinforcement), roadway and drainage (pavement mix designs, RCP, castings, curb and gutter), electrical and traffic (signal foundations, streetlighting, loop detectors, controllers), and specialty (retaining wall, MSE materials, roadside hardware). Review turnaround targets are ten calendar days for first review of major structural submittals and five calendar days for routine submittals, measured from the date of receipt of a complete submittal at Larkspur.
(Normal) 4.5  Task 5 — RFI Response & Design Support
(Normal) Larkspur will log, route, and respond to Requests for Information from the Contractor (Larkspur form RFI-###). Responses that require sealed engineering judgment will be prepared and sealed by the discipline lead of record (structural RFIs by Ms. Raman; roadway and drainage RFIs by the corresponding design leads under Ms. Vasquez's oversight). Target turnaround is five business days from receipt of a complete RFI. RFIs raising Contract interpretation or Contract price and time questions are elevated to Mr. Okafor for coordination with the City Engineer prior to written response.
(Normal) 4.6  Task 6 — Materials Testing Coordination
(Normal) The City will retain an independent materials testing laboratory. Larkspur will coordinate the laboratory's scheduling with the Contractor's operations, receive and log all test reports (concrete cylinder breaks, aggregate sieve analyses, backfill density tests, asphalt density and thickness cores, and specialty tests such as pile driving analyzer records if used), route out-of-specification results for engineering disposition, and file the acceptance record with the pay-application backup. Disposition of out-of-specification results is performed by the discipline lead of record.
(Normal) 4.7  Task 7 — Pay Application & Change Order Certification
(Normal) Larkspur will receive and review monthly Applications for Payment from the Contractor. Each application is reviewed for arithmetical consistency, agreement with the schedule of values, agreement of quantities to date with the daily-report field record, presence of the required documentation for any stored-materials line (bill of sale, off-site insurance, secured storage confirmation) as required by the Contract's stored-materials clause, and correct application of the Contract retainage rate. The Engineer's certification is issued in writing over the Project Manager's signature within seven business days of receipt of a conforming Application for Payment. Change orders proposed by the Contractor or initiated by the City are reviewed for entitlement, quantum, and time, and are logged, tracked to executed status, and reconciled to the running current-Contract-value figure.
(Normal) 4.8  Task 8 — Meetings, Minutes & Coordination
(Normal) Larkspur will attend and lead the weekly construction progress meeting at the field office. Ms. Whitfield chairs the meeting and issues numbered minutes (Larkspur form MEM-###) within three business days of the meeting. Larkspur will also attend the City's monthly project status meetings and other coordination meetings as reasonably requested (utility coordination, floodplain compliance, traffic control coordination). Attendance at City Council briefings is anticipated at four occurrences over the Contract time.
(Normal) 4.9  Task 9

Re: Wren Parkway Widening & Pecan Creek Bridge Replacement — WP-2401
Subject: Time Extension Request & Liquidated-Damages Reservation

Dear Mr. DeLuca:

This letter transmits Vantera Heavy Civil, LLC's formal request for a Time Extension of 21 calendar days to the
Contract and, in connection with that request, Vantera's reservation of rights concerning any assessment of
liquidated damages in the event that final Substantial Completion is not achieved by the currently amended date
of November 20, 2026. This letter is submitted concurrently with, and is supported by, Vantera's written
differing-site-conditions claim of even date and the Contractor's April 2026 monthly quantity report, both of
which are being delivered under separate cover in the same May 8, 2026 consolidated submission.
The Engineer is respectfully requested to review, log, and forward this request to the City for action. Vantera
stands ready to meet at the Engineer's earliest convenience to walk through the supporting record.

1. Basis for the Time Extension Request
The requested 21 calendar days are wholly attributable to conditions encountered in the drilled-shaft foundation
work at Bent 2 of the Pecan Creek bridge replacement. Beginning the week of March 17, 2026, Vantera's drilling
subcontractor encountered materially harder rock, at a higher elevation and over a greater vertical interval, than
what a reasonable and prudent contractor would have anticipated from the contract documents and from the
sealed geotechnical report referenced in the Bid Documents. The impact on production has been documented in
the Engineer's daily reports, in Vantera's shift logs, and in Vantera's Notice under §4.3 dated April 10, 2026.
The critical path of the Project as reflected in Schedule Update 15 (data date April 30, 2026) runs directly through
the Bent 2 shaft cap → column → cap → girder erection → deck pour → approach slab sequence. Any impact to
Bent 2 shaft completion carries day-for-day into the critical path. Vantera's forensic time-impact analysis,
prepared consistent with recognized industry practice, calculates a net delay
to the critical path of 21 calendar days after accounting for concurrent activities and available non-critical
work-around. That analysis is offered without prejudice to any additional entitlement that may develop should the
condition persist beyond the anticipated completion of Bent 2 rock socket drilling.
The direct causes contributing to the 21-calendar-day impact are summarized as follows:
 •   Refusal at higher elevation than indicated. Rock refusal at Bent 2 was reached materially above the
     elevation indicated in the sealed geotechnical record on which Vantera reasonably relied during bidding.
     Detailed elevation data and Vantera's characterization of the encountered condition are set forth in the
     accompanying differing-site-conditions claim letter of even date.

                      Vantera Heavy Civil, LLC · 1800 Industrial Parkway, Bryan, TX 77803 · (979) 555-0166
 Sam DeLuca, PE — Time Extension Request & LD Reservation — May 8, 2026                                          Page 2 of 3


     •   Reduced advance rate through the socket. Rotary drilling advance rates measured across three shift days
         in the week of March 23, 2026 averaged less than one-third of the pre-mobilization production rate assumed
         in Vantera's baseline schedule for a rock socket of the specified depth.
     •   Down-hole tooling change-out. The condition required a change from the initially mobilized rock-auger
         configuration to a core-barrel/roller-cone configuration, together with off-site sharpening cycles that were
         not contemplated by Vantera's baseline production plan.
     •   Weather-window compression. The delay to Bent 2 shaft completion has compressed the working
         window available for the subsequent shaft-cap, column, cap, and girder-erection activities into a period
         during which historically higher rainfall and stream stage on Pecan Creek must be assumed, further
         constraining the recoverable float.
   For the reasons set forth above, and for the reasons set forth in Vantera's differing-site-conditions claim of even
   date, Vantera respectfully requests that a Time Extension of 21 calendar days be added to the Contract Time and
   that the Substantial Completion date be extended accordingly. Vantera reserves the right to supplement this
   request should the condition, or its effects on downstream activities, prove more extensive than the analysis
   presently supports.

   2. Reservation of Rights — Liquidated Damages
   Vantera intends to prosecute the Work diligently and in good faith to achieve Substantial Completion on or before
   the currently amended Substantial Completion date of November 20, 2026. Nothing in this letter should be read
   as a concession that the Contractor will not so achieve, nor as a projection that Substantial Completion will slip.
   Nevertheless, in view of the zero-float condition presently reflected in Schedule Update 15 and in view of the fact
   that the underlying delay events are, in the Contractor's position, the responsibility of the Owner under Contract
   §4.3 and related provisions, Vantera writes to place the City and the Engineer on notice that the Contractor
   expressly reserves all rights against any assessment of liquidated damages that might otherwise be levied should
   Substantial Completion be achieved after November 20, 2026 for reasons attributable, in whole or in part, to the
   Bent 2 condition described in Vantera's differing-site-conditions claim of even date, to any other Owner-caused
   or excusable delay, or to any combination of the foregoing with concurrent contractor-caused activity.
   For the avoidance of doubt, Vantera further notes as follows:
          1. Rate cited. Per Contract Article 4, liquidated damages are assessed at the rate of $1,800 per calendar
          day past Substantial Completion. Vantera reserves the right to challenge any assessment made at that rate,
          or at any other rate, that is inconsistent with the Contractor's position on entitlement to time.
          2. No waiver. No progress payment received by Vantera, no continued prosecution of the Work, no
          attendance at progress meetings, and no submission of schedule updates shall be construed as, or shall
          operate as, a waiver of Vantera's rights against liquidated damages for any portion of the Contract Time
          that becomes the subject of a claim, whether presently pending or hereafter asserted.
          3. Concurrent delay. To the extent that any portion of a delay to Substantial Completion is found to be
          concurrent with an Owner-caused or otherwise excusable delay, Vantera reserves the right to seek relief
          from liquidated damages on a day-for-day basis for that concurrent portion, consistent with recognized
          industry practice for the apportionment of concurrent delay on public works contracts of this size.
          4. Preservation of contract remedies. Nothing in this letter is intended to, or shall be read to, limit,
          modify, or supersede any of the notice, claim, or dispute-resolution provisions of the Contract. Vantera
          reserves all rights and remedies available to it at law, in equity, and under the Contract, all of which are
          expressly preserved.
   Vantera further notes that the Contractor's schedule updates, three-week look-ahead schedules, and short-interval
   plans will continue to reflect a plan to achieve Substantial Completion on or before November 20, 2026,
   notwithstanding this reservation. Should the Engineer disagree, in whole or in part, with any element of Vantera's
   schedule analysis or with Vantera's position with respect to any of the matters set forth above, Vantera requests
   written notice at the earliest opportunity so that the Contractor may respond in a timely fashion.

                         Vantera Heavy Civil, LLC · 1800 Industrial Parkway, Bryan, TX 77803 · (979) 555-0166
 Sam DeLuca, PE — Time Extension Request & LD Reservation — May 8, 2026                                          Page 3 of 3



   3. Requested Action
   Vantera respectfully requests that the Engineer:
     •   Log and acknowledge receipt of this letter in the Project's correspondence register and acknowledge receipt
         in writing;
     •   Review Vantera's Time-Impact Analysis alongside Vantera's differing-site-conditions claim
         of even date and Schedule Update 15 (data date April 30, 2026);
     •   Recommend to the Owner the addition of 21 calendar days to the Contract Time and a corresponding
         revision of the Substantial Completion date; and
     •   Confirm the Owner's position with respect to Vantera's reservation of rights against liquidated damages as




   This letter is submitted under, and pursuant to, the notice and claim provisions of the Contract. Vantera looks
   forward to working with the Engineer and the City toward a prompt and equitable resolution of the matters set
   forth herein.

   Sincerely,
   VANTERA HEAVY CIVIL, LLC

 (Sheet U-04, Rev 1). Franchise-utility records provided by Lone Star Gas Distribution on 02/20/2025, following the

 CO-02 — Justification and Basis for Adjustment

 Excavation for the R-2 wall stem in early April 2025 exposed a zone of soft, high-plasticity clay with intermittent
 organic content, encountered from finished-grade elevation down to an average of 4.8 feet below the theoretical
 bottom-of-wall footing. The condition was not characterized in the Geotechnical Data Report (Redoak Geoscience

Re:  Recommendation of Award — WP-2401 Wren Parkway Widening & Pecan Creek Bridge Replacement
       Federal-Aid Project No. STP 2024(041) MK
Dear Mr. DeLuca:
Larkspur Civil Group, Inc., as Designer of Record and Construction Engineering & Inspection (CEI) consultant for the referenced project, has completed the bid review, arithmetic check, responsiveness determination, and bidder-responsibility investigation for the five bids opened at Milbrook City Hall on November 12, 2024. On the basis of that review, and pursuant to the Instructions to Bidders and the City's procurement ordinance, Larkspur recommends that the City award the WP-2401 construction contract to the apparent low bidder, Vantera Heavy Civil, LLC, in the corrected total amount of $24,618,435.50.
The recommendation is supported by the findings summarized in the sections that follow.
1.  Bid Opening and Enumeration of Bids
Bids were publicly opened and read aloud at 2:00 p.m. Central Time on November 12, 2024, in Conference Room B at Milbrook City Hall. Five sealed bids were received and read. The tabulated totals, after Larkspur's independent extension and footing of each bidder's 118 unit-priced line items against the plan quantities, are:
[TABLE]
Rank | Bidder | Total Bid
1 | Vantera Heavy Civil, LLC | $24,618,435.50
2 | Bluebonnet Construction Co. | $25,412,880.15
3 | Ironhorse Infrastructure LLC | $26,047,220.00
4 | Concho Roadway Builders, Inc. | $26,915,142.60
5 | Summit Heavy Civil, LP | $27,338,995.75
[/TABLE]
Each bid was submitted on the prescribed proposal form, bore the bidder's original signature and corporate seal where applicable, and was accompanied by a 5% bid bond, a Disadvantaged Business Enterprise (DBE) commitment, and the certifications required by the Advertisement for Bids dated October 28, 2024, and by Addendum No. 1 dated November 7, 2024.
2.  Comparison to Engineer's Estimate
Vantera's total of $24,618,435.50 falls squarely within the engineer's-estimate range of $23,000,000 to $26,000,000 carried in the bid tabulation workbook and predicated on the 60% cost estimate transmitted to the City on June 3, 2024, escalated to the advertisement date. The Vantera bid is approximately 0.5% above the midpoint of that range. The two lowest bids (Vantera, Bluebonnet) fall within the advertised range; Ironhorse, Concho, and Summit fall above the upper bound but remain responsive and were investigated for information only.
3.  Arithmetic Verification
Each bidder's unit prices were independently re-multiplied against the plan quantities and totaled by formula in the Larkspur bid-tabulation workbook. No arithmetic errors were found on the Vantera bid; the bidder-submitted total agrees to the penny with Larkspur's workbook foot. The other four bids likewise footed without material discrepancy. No mathematical correction is required to advance the low bidder.
4.  Bidder Responsibility Investigation — Vantera Heavy Civil, LLC
Larkspur conducted the responsibility investigation prescribed by the Instructions to Bidders and by 2 CFR §200.318. The investigation addressed licensure, financial and bonding capacity, project references, safety and integrity, and DBE compliance.
Licensure.  Vantera holds current TxDOT Prequalification No. 51820, verified with the Texas Department of Transportation Contractor and Consultant Management portal on November 18, 2024. The prequalification is in good standing without restriction, suspension, or pending disciplinary action, and its work-class and financial capacity ratings are adequate for the scope and magnitude of WP-2401.
Bonding capacity.  Vantera's surety, a Treasury-listed carrier holding a Texas certificate of authority and rated A (Excellent) by A.M. Best, executed a letter dated November 15, 2024, confirming aggregate bonding capacity of $95,000,000 and single-project capacity of $40,000,000. Both figures exceed the contract amount by the margin required. The surety further confirmed willingness to issue 100% performance and payment bonds on the standard form specified in the contract documents.
Financial capacity.  Vantera provided reviewed year-end financial statements for the two most recent fiscal years, together with a current-work-on-hand schedule. Working capital, net worth, and remaining backlog capacity are consistent with a firm of the size and complexity necessary to prosecute WP-2401 on the schedule advertised.
References.  Larkspur contacted five references furnished by the bidder — three public owners and two prime engineers — covering roadway-widening, bridge-replacement, and drilled-shaft work of comparable scale within the past six years. All five references reported acceptable to strong performance with respect to schedule adherence, submittal quality, subcontractor management, safety, and closeout. No reference reported a terminated contract, a call on a performance or payment bond, or unresolved litigation associated with the referenced project.
Safety and integrity.  The bidder's OSHA 300A summaries, EMR history, and federal debarment records were reviewed. The bidder is not listed in the System for Award Management (SAM.gov) exclusions database, and Vantera executed the certifications required under 2 CFR Part 180 (Nonprocurement Debarment and Suspension), the non-collusion affidavit, and the statutory verifications under Sections 2252.152 (Iran, Sudan, and foreign terrorist organizations) and 2271.002 (boycott of Israel) of the Texas Government Code. Buy America certification was executed as required by the federal-aid program.
Addendum acknowledgment.  Addendum No. 1 (11/07/2024), which reissued Drainage Sheet C-12R (Rev 1), was acknowledged in the Vantera proposal.
On the strength of the above, Vantera Heavy Civil, LLC is determined to be a responsible bidder capable of performing the work in accordance with the contract documents.
5.  DBE Compliance Plan
The contract carries a Disadvantaged Business Enterprise participation goal of 8% for federally assisted work under STP 2024(041) MK. Vantera's DBE commitment package, filed with its bid pursuant to 49 CFR Part 26 and the City's implementing DBE program, identifies certified DBE subcontractors and suppliers whose committed values, taken together, meet the 8% goal on a dollar-value basis measured against the total bid. Each identified DBE firm was verified as certified in the Texas Unified Certification Program (TUCP) directory as of the bid-opening date. The bidder's DBE Affirmative Action Plan, Schedule of DBE Participation, and Letters of Intent are complete and internally consistent. Larkspur therefore concludes that the Vantera DBE plan meets the 8% goal and satisfies the good-faith-effort documentation requirements of the federal program.
6.  Comparison to the Second-Low Bid
The differential between the Vantera bid and the second-low bid (Bluebonnet Construction Co. at $25,412,880.15) is $794,444.65, representing 3.2% of the low bid. That differential is within the range customary for competitively bid unit-price work of this scale and evidences an orderly, competitive bidding market. No indication of unbalanced bidding, front-end loading, or under-priced high-quantity items was identified in the line-item review of the Vantera proposal that would warrant setting aside the low bid or seeking a bid-price justification.
7.  Recommendation
Based on the arithmetic verification, the responsiveness determination, the responsibility investigation, the DBE-plan review, and the relationship of the low bid to the engineer's estimate and to the second-low bid, Larkspur Civil Group, Inc. recommends that the City of Milbrook:
1.  Determine Vantera Heavy Civil, LLC to be the lowest responsive and responsible bidder for WP-2401;
2.  Award the construction contract to Vantera Heavy Civil, LLC in the amount of $24,618,435.50; and
3.  Direct that a Notice of Award be issued upon City Council action, conditioned upon timely execution of the contract agreement, performance and payment bonds each in the full amount of the contract, insurance certificates naming the City as additional insured, and the federal-aid certifications required by the contract documents.
The certified bid tabulation workbook is transmitted herewith; the bidder responsibility file and the DBE commitment package are retained in Larkspur's project record WP-2401-CTR-002.
Should the City require additional information in advance of the Council item, please contact me directly at (512) 555-0184 or mokafor@larkspurcivil.com.
Respectfully submitted,
LARKSPUR CIVIL GROUP, INC.

   Dear Mr. DeLuca:

   Vantera Heavy Civil, LLC (“Vantera,” the Contractor) submits this letter as the formal claim for equitable
   adjustment associated with the differing site condition encountered at Bent 2 of the new Pecan Creek
   Bridge, Sta. 168+95. This claim formalizes and supersedes the written notice of differing site condition
   originally delivered by Vantera to the City and to the Engineer on April 10, 2026, within the notice period
   required by Contract §4.3.

   Vantera has continued to prosecute the work in good faith while the parties evaluate the impacts. This letter
   presents the factual basis for the claim, the contractual basis under Contract §4.3, the quantum of additional
   cost, and the request for a time extension.



   1. Contractual Basis
   Contract §4.3 provides, in relevant part, that the Contractor shall be entitled to an equitable adjustment in the
   Contract Sum and Contract Time where the Contractor encounters subsurface or otherwise concealed
   physical conditions at the Site that are materially different from those indicated in the Contract Documents,
   provided that written notice is given promptly and, in any event, before the conditions are disturbed. Vantera
   provided such written notice by letter dated April 10, 2026, and preserved the physical conditions to the
   extent practicable for the Engineer's inspection on 04/13/2026 and 04/14/2026. This claim is submitted
   timely and in the form required by the Contract.




                   Vantera Heavy Civil, LLC · 1800 Industrial Parkway, Bryan, TX 77803 · (979) 555-0166 · TxDOT PQ 51820
                            May 8, 2026 — Notice of Differing Site Conditions, Bent 2, WP-2401 — Page 1 of 6
 VANTERA HEAVY CIVIL, LLC                                             Notice of Differing Site Conditions — Bent 2, WP-2401 — May 8, 2026


  For the reasons set forth below, Vantera asserts that the condition encountered at Bent 2 constitutes a
  differing site condition within the meaning of §4.3 and that Vantera is entitled to an equitable adjustment in
  the Contract Sum in the amount of $487,600.00 and to a time extension of 21 calendar days.

  2. Contract Documents Relied Upon at Bid
  At the time of bid, Vantera relied upon the following portions of the Contract Documents in preparing its
  estimate for the Bent 2 drilled-shaft installation:

   •   The Foundation Plan, Sheet B-04 , showing the Bent 2 shaft geometry, tip elevation, and required rock
       socket in sound limestone;
   •   The Boring Location Plan bound with the Contract Documents;
   •   The geotechnical report prepared by the Engineer's subconsultant, which was included in the bid
       package and identified as the geotechnical basis of the foundation design;
   •   The technical specifications for drilled-shaft installation, rock excavation, and payment.

  The geotechnical report indicates, at the Bent 2 substructure location, a top-of-rock elevation of
  approximately 524 ft NAVD 88 with the top-of-sound-rock in the general elevation band shown on the
  Contract Documents. In relying on the geotechnical report at bid, Vantera developed unit crew
  productivities and tooling plans consistent with the depth-to-rock and rock-socket lengths represented by the
  Contract Documents.

  Vantera acknowledges the general limitations language customary to geotechnical reporting. That customary
  language does not, however, insulate the Owner from the operation of §4.3 where the actually-encountered
  condition is materially different from what the Contract Documents indicate.

  3. Condition Actually Encountered at Bent 2
  Drilled-shaft installation at Bent 2 was performed by Vantera's foundation crew using an IMT AF200 rotary
  drill with cross-cutter and rock auger tooling appropriate to the anticipated overburden and weathered-rock
  section. Shaft installation at Bent 2 commenced on 03/17/2026 following completion of Bent 1.

  The Bent 2 shaft advanced through overburden without incident to elevation approximately 518.4 ft NAVD
  88, at which point the crew encountered continuous, hard, unweathered limestone requiring a change from
  soil augering to rock-cutting tooling. The elevation at which continuous hard rock was first encountered at
  Bent 2 was surveyed by Vantera's field engineer on 03/17/2026 and independently confirmed on
  03/18/2026. Both measurements place the top of hard rock at 518.4 ft NAVD 88, referenced to the Contract
  vertical datum.

  The condition observed differs from that indicated in the Contract Documents in the following material
  respects:

   1. Elevation of top-of-rock. Top of hard rock at Bent 2 was encountered at 518.4 ft NAVD 88, which is
       approximately 6 feet higher in elevation than the top-of-rock elevation shown in the geotechnical
       report at the Bent 2 substructure location.



                 Vantera Heavy Civil, LLC · 1800 Industrial Parkway, Bryan, TX 77803 · (979) 555-0166 · TxDOT PQ 51820
                          May 8, 2026 — Notice of Differing Site Conditions, Bent 2, WP-2401 — Page 2 of 6
 VANTERA HEAVY CIVIL, LLC                                             Notice of Differing Site Conditions — Bent 2, WP-2401 — May 8, 2026


   2. Character of the rock at the encountered elevation. The rock first encountered was continuous,
       low-RQD-neutral, hard limestone requiring rock-cutter tooling from the initial contact — not the
       weathered-to-transitional profile the Contract Documents indicated would be present at the elevation at
       which rock was first encountered.
   3. Volume of rock excavation. The additional 6 vertical feet of rock, over the plan shaft diameter and
       across both shafts at Bent 2, materially increased the quantity of rock excavation required to reach the
       plan tip elevation compared to the quantity indicated by the Contract Documents.

  The 03/17/2026 daily inspection report prepared by the Engineer's field representative independently notes
  “hard drilling encountered above the anticipated top-of-rock elevation” at Bent 2, corroborating Vantera's
  observation.

  Vantera's field observations, the survey measurements taken on 03/17/2026 and 03/18/2026, and the
  rock-elevation survey data collectively establish that the encountered condition
  was materially different from those indicated in the Contract Documents. Accordingly, the encountered
  condition constitutes a differing site condition within the meaning of Contract §4.3.

  4. Impact on the Work
  The differing site condition impacted the Bent 2 shaft installation in the following respects:

  4.1 Additional rock drilling.
  The unanticipated 6 ft of hard-rock section above the elevation indicated by the Contract Documents
  required Vantera to drill an additional volume of rock at each of the Bent 2 shafts to reach the plan tip
  elevation. Rock drilling productivity in the encountered material was substantially lower than the
  productivity assumed at bid for the elevations in question, and the additional volume was not included in the
  bid quantities on which Vantera priced the drilled-shaft pay item.

  4.2 Tooling changes and wear.
  The encountered condition required Vantera to mobilize a supplemental rock-cutter head and a second set of
  teeth mid-shaft, and to demobilize and re-sharpen tooling twice within the Bent 2 sequence. Tooling wear
  costs incurred are substantially in excess of the tooling wear anticipated at bid for the Bent 2 shafts.

  4.3 Crew standby and re-sequencing.
  The change from soil-augering to rock-cutting mid-shaft, coupled with the additional tooling change
  described above, required the shaft crew to stand by while tooling was exchanged and re-sharpened, and
  required the concrete-placement subcontractor to be re-sequenced twice.

  4.4 Delay to the Bent 2 completion milestone.
  The additional rock drilling, tooling exchanges, and re-sequencing delayed the Bent 2 shaft completion
  milestone by 21 calendar days from the baseline schedule. Because Bent 2 is on the critical path for the
  substructure completion and for the subsequent superstructure erection, the delay to Bent 2 flows through
  directly to project Substantial Completion.

  5. Cost Claim

 VANTERA HEAVY CIVIL, LLC                                              Notice of Differing Site Conditions — Bent 2, WP-2401 — May 8, 2026


  Vantera has priced the impacts described in Section 4 in accordance with the cost principles of the Contract.
  The claimed additional cost is summarized below by cost element, reflecting Vantera's crew time, tooling,
  and equipment costs for the impacts described in Section 4.

   Additional rock drilling — labor and equipment                                                                     214,800
   Rock-cutter tooling, teeth, and re-sharpening                                                                          68,400
   Crew standby during tooling exchanges                                                                                  41,200
   Concrete-placement subcontractor re-sequencing                                                                         22,600
   Field engineering, survey re-shots, and QA/QC                                                                          14,900
   Time-related field overhead (21 days)                                                                                  76,300
   Time-related home-office overhead (21 days, Eichleay-basis, per Contract)                                              28,700
   Subtotal                                                                                                           466,900
   Bond and insurance markup (per Contract)                                                                                6,900
   Contractor markup on direct cost (per Contract)                                                                        13,800
   Total requested equitable adjustment                                                                              $487,600

  Vantera has excluded from this claim any cost that is not properly a consequence of the differing site
  condition, and any cost element already recovered under a separate change order or pay application.



  6. Time Claim
  Vantera requests an equitable adjustment in the Contract Time in the amount of 21 additional calendar
  days, extending the currently scheduled Substantial Completion date accordingly. The 21-day duration is
  supported by Vantera's schedule fragnet analysis and is measured from the baseline Bent 2
  shaft-completion activity in the current approved schedule to the actual Bent 2
  shaft-completion date recorded in Vantera's field records. The delay is on the critical path and is neither
  concurrent with nor caused by any Contractor-caused delay.

  7. Notice and Preservation
  Written notice of the differing site condition was given by Vantera to the City and to the Engineer on April
  10, 2026, within the notice period required by Contract §4.3. The physical conditions were preserved to the
  extent practicable for inspection by the Engineer; the Engineer's field representative inspected the Bent 2
  shaft on 04/13/2026 and again on 04/14/2026 and observed the encountered material.


  Vantera has continued to prosecute the work diligently during the pendency of this claim and reserves all
  rights under the Contract and applicable law.

  8. Requested Action
